connectorUiConfig.title: HoneyForge Threat Detection
connectorUiConfig.descriptionMarkdown:
The [HoneyForge](https://honeyforge.tech) connector ingests deception sensor events from the HoneyForge Threat Detection Platform into Microsoft Sentinel. HoneyForge deploys hardware honeypot sensors across your network that passively listen for connection attempts. Any interaction with a sensor is, by definition, suspicious — because legitimate systems should never communicate with a decoy device.

Events are forwarded to Microsoft Sentinel in Common Event Format (CEF) via syslog. The connector provides immediate detection coverage through the bundled analytic rule, hunting queries, and operational workbook.

sampleQueries.query:
CommonSecurityLog
| where DeviceVendor =~ "BUI"
| where DeviceProduct =~ "HoneyForge"
| where TimeGenerated >= ago(24h)
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

sampleQueries.description: Top source IPs interacting with sensors — last 7 days

| where DeviceVendor =~ "BUI"
| where DeviceProduct =~ "HoneyForge"
| where TimeGenerated >= ago(7d)
| summarize EventCount = count() by SourceIP
| top 20 by EventCount desc

CommonSecurityLog
| where DeviceVendor =~ "BUI"
| where DeviceProduct =~ "HoneyForge"
| where TimeGenerated >= ago(7d)
| extend SensorName = iff(isempty(tostring(DeviceCustomString3)), tostring(Computer), tostring(DeviceCustomString3))
| summarize EventCount = count() by SensorName
| sort by EventCount desc

| summarize LastLogReceived = max(TimeGenerated)

The **Common Event Format (CEF) via AMA** solution must be installed in your Microsoft Sentinel workspace. [Install from Microsoft Marketplace](https://marketplace.microsoft.com/en-us/product/saas/azuresentinel.azure-sentinel-solution-commoneventformat)

instructionSteps.description: >**NOTE:** This connector uses the **Common Event Format (CEF)** to forward HoneyForge sensor events to Microsoft Sentinel via syslog. An ASIM parser (`HoneyForgeEvent`) is deployed with this solution to normalise the events to the ASIM NetworkSession schema.

Deploy a Linux machine to act as the syslog forwarder between your HoneyForge deployment and Microsoft Sentinel. This machine can be on-premises, in Azure, or in another cloud. It must have network line-of-sight to receive syslog from HoneyForge and outbound HTTPS to the Log Analytics workspace.

**Requirements:**
- Python 2.7 or 3.x
- sudo / elevated permissions
- Outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) to `*.ods.opinsights.azure.com`
- Inbound TCP/UDP 514 from the HoneyForge backend

innerSteps.title: 1.1 — Install the Log Analytics agent and CEF collector
innerSteps.description: Run the following command on your Linux forwarder machine. Replace `{WorkspaceId}` and `{PrimaryKey}` with your Microsoft Sentinel workspace values.

parameters.label: Run on the Linux forwarder:
parameters.value: sudo wget -O cef_installer.py https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/master/DataConnectors/CEF/cef_installer.py && sudo python cef_installer.py {0} {1}

instructionSteps.title: Step 1 — Deploy the CEF syslog forwarder

instructionSteps.description:
Configure HoneyForge to forward CEF-formatted sensor events to the Linux forwarder.

1. Log in to the HoneyForge dashboard at [platform.honeyforge.tech](https://platform.honeyforge.tech).
2. Navigate to **Settings → SIEM / Syslog**.
3. Enter the **IP address** of your Linux forwarder and port **514**.
4. Select **CEF** as the format and save.
5. Click **Send test event** to verify connectivity.

For assistance configuring syslog forwarding, contact BUI at [support@bui.co.za](mailto:support@bui.co.za).
instructionSteps.title: Step 2 — Configure HoneyForge syslog forwarding

instructionSteps.description:
Allow up to 20 minutes for the first events to appear in the `CommonSecurityLog` table. Validate that events are arriving with the following query:

```kql
CommonSecurityLog
| where DeviceVendor =~ "BUI"
| where DeviceProduct =~ "HoneyForge"
| take 10
```

If no events appear after 20 minutes, run the connectivity troubleshooter:

parameters.label: Run the troubleshooter on the Linux forwarder:
parameters.value: sudo wget -O cef_troubleshoot.py https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/master/DataConnectors/CEF/cef_troubleshoot.py && sudo python cef_troubleshoot.py {0}

instructionSteps.title: Step 3 — Validate connectivity

properties.description:
Detects an interaction with a HoneyForge deception sensor. Any activity
involving a HoneyForge sensor must be treated as potentially unauthorised
until validated by the security operations team.

HoneyForge sensors are passive decoy devices  - legitimate systems and users
should never communicate with them. Any detected interaction may indicate
network scanning, lateral movement, or an actively compromised device.
properties.query:
CommonSecurityLog
| where DeviceVendor =~ "BUI"
| where DeviceProduct =~ "HoneyForge"
| extend
    SrcIpAddr = tostring(SourceIP),
    DstIpAddr = tostring(DestinationIP),
    SensorID = tostring(DeviceCustomString1),
    CustomerID = tostring(DeviceCustomString2),
    SensorName = iff(
        isempty(tostring(DeviceCustomString3)),
        tostring(Computer),
        tostring(DeviceCustomString3)
    ),
    EventType = iff(
        isempty(tostring(DeviceEventClassID)),
        "unknown",
        tostring(DeviceEventClassID)
    ),
    EventActivity = tostring(Activity),
    EventProtocol = tostring(Protocol)
| where isnotempty(SrcIpAddr)
| where isnotempty(DstIpAddr)
| summarize
    TimeGenerated = max(TimeGenerated),
    FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
    EventCount = count(),
    SourcePorts = make_set(tostring(SourcePort), 20),
    DestinationPorts = make_set(tostring(DestinationPort), 20),
    Protocols = make_set(EventProtocol, 10),
    Activities = make_set(EventActivity, 20),
    CEFSeverities = make_set(tostring(LogSeverity), 10),
    DeviceVersions = make_set(tostring(DeviceVersion), 10),
    Collectors = make_set(tostring(Computer), 10)
    by
        SrcIpAddr,
        DstIpAddr,
        SensorID,
        CustomerID,
        SensorName,
        EventType
| extend
    SourcePortList = strcat_array(SourcePorts, ", "),
    DestinationPortList = strcat_array(DestinationPorts, ", "),
    ProtocolList = strcat_array(Protocols, ", "),
    ActivityList = strcat_array(Activities, ", "),
    CEFSeverityList = strcat_array(CEFSeverities, ", "),
    DeviceVersionList = strcat_array(DeviceVersions, ", "),
    CollectorList = strcat_array(Collectors, ", ")
| project
    TimeGenerated,
    FirstSeen,
    LastSeen,
    EventCount,
    SrcIpAddr,
    DstIpAddr,
    SourcePortList,
    DestinationPortList,
    ProtocolList,
    SensorID,
    SensorName,
    CustomerID,
    EventType,
    ActivityList,
    CEFSeverityList,
    DeviceVersionList,
    CollectorList

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat:
HoneyForge detected {{EventCount}} event(s) targeting {{DstIpAddr}}
using {{ProtocolList}}. Treat this activity as unauthorised until validated.

properties.description: HoneyForge_FleetCoverage_HuntingQueries Hunting Query with template version 3.0.3

properties.displayName: HoneyForge - Sensor Fleet Coverage and Health
properties.query:
let lookback = 30d;
let offlineThreshold = 10m;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated >= ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "BUI"
| where DeviceProduct =~ "HoneyForge"
| extend
    SensorID   = tostring(DeviceCustomString1),
    CustomerID = tostring(DeviceCustomString2),
    SensorName = iff(isempty(tostring(DeviceCustomString3)), tostring(Computer), tostring(DeviceCustomString3))
| summarize
    TotalEvents     = count(),
    UniqueSources   = dcount(SourceIP),
    FirstEvent      = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastEvent       = max(TimeGenerated),
    Protocols       = make_set(tostring(Protocol), 10)
    by SensorID, SensorName, CustomerID
| extend
    MinutesSinceLast = datetime_diff('minute', now(), LastEvent),
    SensorStatus     = iff(datetime_diff('minute', now(), LastEvent) <= 10, "Online", "Offline / No Recent Events"),
    ProtocolStr      = strcat_array(Protocols, ", ")
| sort by SensorStatus asc, LastEvent desc
| project
    SensorName,
    SensorID,
    CustomerID,
    SensorStatus,
    MinutesSinceLast,
    TotalEvents,
    UniqueSources,
    FirstEvent,
    LastEvent,
    ProtocolStr

tags.name: description
tags.value:
Provides a per-sensor event summary for the past 30 days, giving visibility
into which sensors are active, which are quiet, and which may be offline or
misconfigured (no events in the last 10 minutes is the offline threshold).

Use this query during routine operations to confirm full fleet coverage and
identify any gaps in your deception layer before an attacker does.

properties.displayName: HoneyForge - Sensor Fleet Coverage and Health

properties.description: HoneyForge_HighFrequency_HuntingQueries Hunting Query with template version 3.0.3

properties.query:
let lookback = 24h;
let burstWindow = 10m;
let burstThreshold = 50;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated >= ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "BUI"
| where DeviceProduct =~ "HoneyForge"
| extend
    SrcIpAddr  = tostring(SourceIP),
    SensorName = iff(isempty(tostring(DeviceCustomString3)), tostring(Computer), tostring(DeviceCustomString3)),
    CustomerID = tostring(DeviceCustomString2)
| where isnotempty(SrcIpAddr)
| summarize
    BurstCount    = count(),
    SensorsHit    = dcount(SensorName),
    SensorList    = make_set(SensorName, 10),
    Protocols     = make_set(tostring(Protocol), 5),
    DestPorts     = make_set(tostring(DestinationPort), 10),
    WindowStart   = min(TimeGenerated),
    WindowEnd     = max(TimeGenerated)
    by SrcIpAddr, CustomerID, bin(TimeGenerated, burstWindow)
| where BurstCount >= burstThreshold
| extend
    SensorListStr = strcat_array(SensorList, ", "),
    ProtocolStr   = strcat_array(Protocols, ", "),
    DestPortStr   = strcat_array(DestPorts, ", ")
| sort by BurstCount desc
| project
    SrcIpAddr,
    CustomerID,
    BurstCount,
    SensorsHit,
    WindowStart,
    WindowEnd,
    SensorListStr,
    ProtocolStr,
    DestPortStr

tags.name: description
tags.value:
Detects source IPs generating an unusually high volume of events against
HoneyForge sensors in a short window (more than 50 events in any 10-minute
period). This pattern is characteristic of automated scanners, brute-force
tools, or worm-like lateral movement.

High-frequency hits deserve immediate triage  - especially if the source is
an internal IP, which would indicate a compromised or misconfigured device
inside the network.

properties.query:
let lookback = 7d;
let businessStart = 7;   // 07:00 UTC
let businessEnd   = 19;  // 19:00 UTC
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated >= ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "BUI"
| where DeviceProduct =~ "HoneyForge"
| extend
    SrcIpAddr  = tostring(SourceIP),
    SensorName = iff(isempty(tostring(DeviceCustomString3)), tostring(Computer), tostring(DeviceCustomString3)),
    CustomerID = tostring(DeviceCustomString2),
    HourUTC    = hourofday(TimeGenerated),
    DayOfWeek  = dayofweek(TimeGenerated)
| extend
    IsOffHours = case(
        // Weekend (Saturday = 6d, Sunday = 0d)
        DayOfWeek == 0d or DayOfWeek == 6d, true,
        // Outside business hours on weekdays
        HourUTC < businessStart or HourUTC >= businessEnd, true,
        false
    )
| where IsOffHours == true
| where isnotempty(SrcIpAddr)
| summarize
    TotalEvents   = count(),
    SensorsHit    = dcount(SensorName),
    SensorList    = make_set(SensorName, 20),
    FirstSeen     = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen      = max(TimeGenerated),
    HoursActive   = make_set(HourUTC, 24),
    Protocols     = make_set(tostring(Protocol), 10)
    by SrcIpAddr, CustomerID
| sort by TotalEvents desc
| extend
    SensorListStr = strcat_array(SensorList, ", "),
    ProtocolStr   = strcat_array(Protocols, ", "),
    HoursStr      = strcat_array(todynamic(tostring(HoursActive)), ", ")
| project
    SrcIpAddr,
    CustomerID,
    TotalEvents,
    SensorsHit,
    FirstSeen,
    LastSeen,
    HoursStr,
    SensorListStr,
    ProtocolStr

tags.name: description
tags.value:
Surfaces HoneyForge sensor interactions that occurred outside normal business
hours (before 07:00 or after 19:00 UTC, Monday to Friday, and all day on
weekends). Off-hours activity from internal IPs is especially suspicious  -
it may indicate a compromised device operating autonomously or an insider
threat.

Adjust the hour thresholds to match your organisation's working hours if
they differ from the defaults.

properties.description: HoneyForge_RepeatedProbes_HuntingQueries Hunting Query with template version 3.0.3

properties.displayName: HoneyForge - Repeated Probes from Same Source
properties.query:
let lookback = 14d;
let minSessionGap = 1h;
let minReturnVisits = 2;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated >= ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "BUI"
| where DeviceProduct =~ "HoneyForge"
| extend
    SrcIpAddr  = tostring(SourceIP),
    SensorName = iff(isempty(tostring(DeviceCustomString3)), tostring(Computer), tostring(DeviceCustomString3))
| where isnotempty(SrcIpAddr)
| sort by SrcIpAddr asc, TimeGenerated asc
| serialize
| extend
    PrevTime = prev(TimeGenerated, 1),
    PrevSrc  = prev(SrcIpAddr, 1)
| extend
    IsNewSession = iff(SrcIpAddr == PrevSrc and (TimeGenerated - PrevTime) < minSessionGap, 0, 1)
| summarize
    TotalEvents   = count(),
    SessionCount  = sumif(IsNewSession, IsNewSession == 1),
    SensorsHit    = dcount(SensorName),
    FirstSeen     = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen      = max(TimeGenerated),
    SensorList    = make_set(SensorName, 20)
    by SrcIpAddr
| where SessionCount >= minReturnVisits
| extend DaySpan = datetime_diff('day', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| sort by SessionCount desc, TotalEvents desc
| extend SensorListStr = strcat_array(SensorList, ", ")
| project
    SrcIpAddr,
    SessionCount,
    TotalEvents,
    SensorsHit,
    DaySpan,
    FirstSeen,
    LastSeen,
    SensorListStr

tags.name: description
tags.value:
Finds source IPs that have probed HoneyForge sensors on multiple distinct
occasions separated by at least one hour, suggesting deliberate or scripted
reconnaissance rather than a one-off event.

A legitimate network scanner that hits a sensor once might be an
oversight. One that returns hours or days later is a persistent threat.

properties.displayName: HoneyForge - Repeated Probes from Same Source

properties.query:
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated >= ago(7d)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "BUI"
| where DeviceProduct =~ "HoneyForge"
| extend
    SrcIpAddr   = tostring(SourceIP),
    SensorName  = iff(isempty(tostring(DeviceCustomString3)), tostring(Computer), tostring(DeviceCustomString3)),
    CustomerID  = tostring(DeviceCustomString2)
| where isnotempty(SrcIpAddr)
| summarize
    TotalEvents      = count(),
    SensorsHit       = dcount(SensorName),
    CustomersAffected = dcount(CustomerID),
    FirstSeen        = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen         = max(TimeGenerated),
    SensorList       = make_set(SensorName, 20),
    Protocols        = make_set(tostring(Protocol), 10),
    DestPorts        = make_set(tostring(DestinationPort), 20)
    by SrcIpAddr
| sort by TotalEvents desc
| extend
    SensorListStr  = strcat_array(SensorList, ", "),
    ProtocolStr    = strcat_array(Protocols, ", "),
    DestPortStr    = strcat_array(DestPorts, ", ")
| project
    SrcIpAddr,
    TotalEvents,
    SensorsHit,
    CustomersAffected,
    FirstSeen,
    LastSeen,
    SensorListStr,
    ProtocolStr,
    DestPortStr

tags.name: description
tags.value:
Identifies the source IP addresses that have interacted most frequently with
HoneyForge deception sensors over the past 7 days. Repeat offenders across
multiple sensors are especially high-priority  - they indicate persistent
reconnaissance or an automated scanner that missed the exclusion list.

Use this query as a starting point for threat-intel enrichment and to decide
which IPs warrant a block rule or further investigation.
